slides.purpose: Frame extensions as selected local or structural repairs rather than an inevitable ladder.
slides.successCheck: Reader asks what failed, what kind of repair is wanted, and what must be preserved.

slides.purpose: Inline the natural-number convention and repair 2−5 with additive inverses.
slides.successCheck: Reader reconstructs 2−5=2+(−5)=−3 and identifies preservation of prior addition and order as a chosen constraint.

slides.purpose: Repair 2x=1 while explaining integer parity, the zero-inverse boundary, and equivalent fraction names.
slides.successCheck: Reader explains why 2x is never 1 in ℤ, why zero has no inverse, and why 1/2=2/4.

slides.purpose: Show that rational addition is independent of representatives, first by one check and then in general.
slides.successCheck: Reader verifies 5/6=10/12 and derives (ad+bc)b'd'=(a'd'+b'c')bd from ab'=a'b and cd'=c'd.

slides.purpose: Expose an exact missing length and earn its irrationality on the required path before distinguishing adjoining one root from constructing all reals.
slides.successCheck: Reader uses odd squares and p²=2q² to force numerator and denominator even, identifies the reduced-fraction contradiction, and distinguishes the local ℚ(√2) repair from the global real requirement.

slides.purpose: Contrast one generated-field repair with a boundary property required for every eligible set, using only density of ℚ in ℝ on the mainline.
slides.successCheck: Reader distinguishes density in ℝ from completeness and local repair from the universal least-upper-bound requirement.

slides.purpose: Define upper bound, least upper bound, and maximum before stating the ordered-field and existence/uniqueness packages.
slides.successCheck: Reader states both quantifiers in the least-upper-bound definition, explains why a supremum need not lie in the set, and knows the article takes existence from a separate construction rather than performing it.

slides.purpose: Show that ordered real arithmetic cannot solve x²=−1.
slides.successCheck: Reader closes all sign cases using the positive-product law and identifies the new algebraic goal.

slides.purpose: Construct the complex field operations and nonzero inverses on real pairs.
slides.successCheck: Reader identifies 0 and 1, checks i²=−1, and verifies the inverse formula using a²+b²>0.

slides.purpose: Interpret multiplication by i through one exact coordinate and norm calculation.
slides.successCheck: Reader maps (2,−1) to (1,2), checks equal squared lengths, and handles zero separately.

slides.purpose: Answer the opening through local/global repair choices and conditional structure theorems.
slides.successCheck: Reader explains why neither ℝ nor ℂ is forced by one obstruction and why proper extensions need not preserve every property.

slides.purpose: Make the nonzero-denominator domain part of the quotient construction.
slides.successCheck: Reader reconstructs the (0,0) counterexample to transitivity of the naively enlarged relation.

slides.purpose: Prove transitivity without presupposing rational division.
slides.successCheck: Reader derives d(af−be)=0 and applies the no-zero-divisors property of ℤ with d≠0.

slides.purpose: Prove the parity lemma and begin the reduced-fraction contradiction.
slides.successCheck: Reader derives odd n=2k+1 ⇒ n²=4k(k+1)+1 and then p² even ⇒ p even.

slides.purpose: Complete the second parity branch.
slides.successCheck: Reader proves q is even and identifies the contradiction with gcd(p,q)=1 while preserving the separate existence assumption.

slides.purpose: Make the ambient ordered universe control eligible bounds.
slides.successCheck: Reader explains why √2 is eligible in ℝ but not ℚ and why this comparison diagnoses ℚ rather than constructs ℝ.

slides.purpose: Eliminate every rational least-upper-bound candidate.
slides.successCheck: Reader handles r≤0, 0<r<√2, r=√2, and r>√2 without skipping a case.

slides.purpose: Derive unboundedness of the natural-number copy from the least-upper-bound property.
slides.successCheck: Reader starts from s=sup ℕ and obtains the contradiction s<n+1∈ℕ.

slides.purpose: Prove the generic ordered-field integer-part lemma and then rational density.
slides.successCheck: Reader uses well-ordering on {k∈ℕ:k>z+N} to obtain z<m≤z+1, then derives x<m/n<y from n(y−x)>1.

slides.purpose: Define the cut map only after proving its source set nonempty and bounded, then prove strict order with two rationals.
slides.successCheck: Reader chooses m<x<n and x<r<s<y, identifies rG as an upper bound of the defining set, and reconstructs φ(x)≤rG<sG≤φ(y).

slides.purpose: Prove that the cut map fixes every rational and establish the rational comparison equivalence.
slides.successCheck: Reader proves φ(aF)=aG and qF<x iff qG<φ(x), including one inserted rational in the forward direction.

slides.purpose: Construct an inverse element from the lower rational cut of a target element.
slides.successCheck: Reader proves q<x iff qG<y, including the extra-rational step, and concludes φ(x)=y.

slides.purpose: Prove order isomorphisms preserve suprema, then preserve addition and multiplication through rational sets cofinal against arbitrary field elements.
slides.successCheck: Reader proves the supremum transport lemma, constructs sum/product approximants for arbitrary u in F and G, derives φ(−x)=−φ(x), and covers zero and every sign case.

slides.purpose: Justify the eventual-sign total order on a proper non-Archimedean field extension and clarify the separate complex-coefficient example.
slides.successCheck: Reader explains leading-coefficient eventual signs, closure of the positive cone under addition and multiplication, derives t>n, rejects least-upper-bound completeness, and treats ℂ(t) as independently derived.

slides.purpose: Prove the exact order structure unavailable on ℂ.
slides.successCheck: Reader closes both i>0 and −i>0 branches without banning arbitrary comparisons.

slides.purpose: Compare the ordered-complete and algebraic-extension property bundles.
slides.successCheck: Reader states the hypotheses needed for real-field uniqueness and the algebraic gain/order cost of ℂ.
